articles.title: NFL today: How to watch Cowboys v Packers, TV channels & live stream Sunday 18 October
articles.summary: How will the Dallas and Green Bay fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream options. articles.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
articles.summary: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different. At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada, looking down pensively…
body: Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble.

How do you solve what is, on revenue versus results, the worst-run club in world football? By changing the name of the latest patsy on the touchline, of course. For now a hard-fought point is perhaps enough to stave off that pre-programmed emergency response.

Stand down the cowboy cops. Call off the blue and white saloons. Although with a run of Bournemouth, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool next up in the league it will no doubt soon be time to go out there and arrest Lee Harvey Oswald again. What’s that you say? OK, well, dig him up again. Re-arrest him. Whatever it takes. Someone has to stop these lone gunmen, these managerial magic bullet merchants from derailing the Manchester United supremacy.

Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different.

articles.title: European football: 10-man Lyon hold off Nice to move top of Ligue 1
articles.summary: Five teams level on points after Monaco lose to Lorient. Real Madrid ease past Sevilla with Mbappé double. Ten-man Lyon held on for a 2-1 comeback victory over Nice to move top of Ligue 1 on Sunday, as previous pacesetters Monaco lost for the first time this season.
body: It was a close run affair for Lyon, playing in front of local boy and French cycling prodigy Paul Seixas, following Keito Nakamura’s dismissal 20 minutes from time.
Côte d’Ivoire forward Elye Wahi, who opened the scoring for Nice on 18 minutes with his second goal of the season, was denied a stoppage-time equaliser by a tight offside call.
Two goals in three minutes turned the game around by half-time as Pavel Sulc equalised by prodding home a rebound and Tanner Tessmann headed the hosts in front.
Veteran Belgium midfielder Axel Witsel headed against the bar early in the second half while Wahi hit the post with a close-range header, shortly after Nakamura was dismissed for a high boot.

articles.title: Madueke breaks Nottingham Forest’s resistance as dogged Arsenal edge to victory
articles.summary: The theme before kick-off was blanks. Or, more precisely, whether either team could stop firing them at the City Ground. It was a detail to make Oliver Glasner extremely uncomfortable that his Nottingham Forest team had still to score at their own stadium this season.
body: Forest’s frustrations under their new manager go on. It was another spirited performance from them, bits to like, especially a full-throttle performance from Liam Delap in the No 9 position. But, for the fifth time under Glasner, there was not a goal to celebrate in front of the home support.

It was a game that came to feel increasingly set up for the famous terrace chant. One-nil to the Ars-en-nal. Or, as the travelling hordes would have it, one-nil to the champions. Arsenal did not play well. They created little, finishing with just one shot on target. How Noni Madueke made it count.

On as a half-time substitute, the winger took a pass from Declan Rice in the 80th minute and had only one thing on his mind. To cut inside from the left and unload. The connection was pure and that was when he caught a break, which he has worked to earn after a difficult start to the season. The ball deflected off Jair Cunha and flew past the Forest goalkeeper, Matz Sels.

articles.title: 'Four points is nothing' - O'Neill stays cool after statement win
articles.summary: Amid supporter discontent, a recent protest against the major shareholder and a veteran manager deciding now is not the time to "wrap things up", as Martin O'Neill put it, you'd be forgiven for scratching your head when examining Celtic's current domestic situation.
body: They sit four points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership. Five, really, if you factor in a goal difference at present 12 better than nearest challengers Rangers.

All this off the back of a 7-1 demolition of last season's runners-up, Hearts, who - at least until they turned up at Celtic Park - were widely viewed as viable title contenders if there's to be another three-way fight for Scottish football's main prize.
Has normal service been restored in the east end of Glasgow after the wobbles of four significant defeats in their past half-dozen? Not as far as their wily old manager is concerned.

Keen to stress that the road is yet long to the division's ultimate destination, O'Neill was full of smiles after his side's biggest win since he returned last year, but he didn't even accept that such a thrashing of the third-placed side in the division was even a 'statement' victory.

articles.title: Texas Tech makes impression on EDGE Jaylen Johnson
articles.summary: Roeland Park (Kans.) Bishop Miege EDGE Jaylen Johnson got down to Texas Tech for a visit over the weekend. Following the trip, which included Johnson seeing the Red Raiders go to 6-0 with a 28-point win over Arizona State, it is clear they will be a school in high consideration in this recruitment.
body: “Texas Tech is a great place, man,” Johnson said. “I got a quick tour of the facilities along with campus, and I had a chance to talk with Coach Jac Smith, the outside linebackers coach. He was honest with me, and I really liked the way he carried himself with my family.”
“Coach Blanchard was super cordial to me and my family, and I loved everything about him as a person,” Johnson said.
He added, “The game against Arizona State was also great because of their win in dominating fashion.”
Johnson has been to Kansas and Kansas State, and those in-state schools are two other top schools in the recruitment. He is visiting Iowa State coming up.

articles.title: 'Pure relief' as St Brigid's claim first Antrim title
articles.summary: Joseph Finnegan, JJ Higgins and Jack Dowling react to St Brigid's historic first Antrim SFC title after they beat O'Donovan Rossa in the decider.
body: "Pure relief" was the overriding feeling of many St Brigid's players as the final whistle sounded to confirm their 0-21 to 1-16 win Antrim final over O'Donovan Rossa, which secured their first ever senior football title.

The south Belfast club, founded in 1998, were gracing the Antrim decider for the first time and recovered from a nervy start at Corrigan Park to make history as they finally got their hands on Padraig McNamee Cup.
They fought back from trailing 0-7 to 0-3 at one stage of the first half to lead by two at the break in the all-Belfast decider.

Cathal Murray's side, inspired by teenager JJ Higgins, who kicked seven points, held their nerve in the second half, despite a Rossa goal, to win by two and spark a blue and yellow pitch invasion at full-time.

McConkey has struggled with injuries, which have included a rib injury, ankle injury, and now a concussion.
McConkey should not be dropped in the wake of his injury, and the Chargers have a Week 7 bye, which should give the receiver enough time to recover.

articles.title: De Zerbi reveals ban in latest bid to lift Spurs spirit: 'You try to find all solutions'
articles.summary: Roberto De Zerbi has revealed a ban he put in place phones during Tottenham’s warm weather training camp in Marbella in his latest attempt to improve the camp’s spirit.
body: Spurs committed more than £380million on new signings this summer with 10 players joining, but they will start Monday’s home fixture with Coventry at the bottom of the Premier League.
The manager has revealed he banned phones from mealtime during Tottenham’s trip to Marbella.
“We worked on the pitch, we stayed together – we removed phones from breakfast, lunch and dinner to stay together because now it is like (phone) all the time,” De Zerbi told a press conference.

“We had two or three important meetings speaking about football, our situation and how everyone has to take responsibility. And nothing more. There were some dinners just for the players, some dinners just for the staff.

articles.title: Arsenal win with one shot on target as Forest sink into bottom three
articles.summary: Arsenal's only shot on target proved enough to snatch victory at Nottingham Forest through Noni Madueke's deflected strike, keeping the champions within touching distance of Premier League leaders Manchester City and condemning Forest to the relegation zone.
body: After 80 frustrating minutes at the City Ground, substitute Madueke cut inside from the left and fired towards goal. His strike deflected off Jair Cunha, wrong-footed Matz Sels and found the net to settle a game in which Arsenal had struggled to turn possession into chances.

Arsenal had dominated the ball but registered no shots on target in the first half. Kai Havertz headed wide from a Declan Rice free-kick while Gabriel's set-piece effort was cleared almost off the line by Ousmane Diomande.

Forest made life difficult for Mikel Arteta's side, defending resolutely and threatening on the counter. Murillo almost salvaged a point in stoppage time with a superb solo run, driving at the Arsenal defence before curling narrowly wide. Ezri Konsa then made a crucial late challenge to deny Liam Delap.
However, despite their opportunities, it was the same old story for Oliver Glasner's side, who failed to find a breakthrough.

articles.title: Texans beat Jags in final seconds of Wembley thriller
articles.summary: Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked a 49-yard field goal as time expired to lift the Houston Texans to a 34-31 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in a thriller at Wembley Stadium on Sunday.
body: It was a game that began with referee Larry Smith being carted off with a non-contact injury in the opening seconds. A game that spent its interval staging on-field Corgi races. And a game that concluded with another dose of boot-fuelled drama following Cam Little's last-second winner against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham the previous week.
Texans quarterback CJ Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns while Jaylin Noel led his side with four receptions for 107 yards and a score as Houston improved to 2-4 on the year.

Stroud's first interception of the season came by way of Travis Hunter as the two-way Jags star became the first player to score a touchdown and record a pick in the same game since Brian Dawkins for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Texans on September 29, 2002.
Trevor Lawrence finished 24 of 41 for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one interception as the Jaguars slipped to 4-2 at the end of their fortnight in the UK.
